records.public_safe_text: unit # 1 was sitting at a red light facing westbound in the [roadway]. driver of unit # 1 stated that the light turned green and she entered the intersection. the pedestrian was on the southwest corner of the intersection and began walking east across the intersection. the pedestrian was then struck by unit # 1 [roadway] [roadway]. driver of unit # 1 stated that she saw a red hand for the cross walk and did not see the pedestrian until right before impact. driver of unit # 1 stated that she was going 5mph or less. the pedestrian stated that he had pressed the cross walk button and when the light changed he began crossing the intersection and was struck by unit # 1. the pedestrian advised that this was the only intersection that he had used the cross walk button. officer is unable to determine if the cross walk button was pushed or not. each subject involved is saying something different. officer does know that if the cross walk button is not pushed that it will not give the pedestrian a white walking symbol. the button has to be pushed at the intersection to give the walk symbol. officer spoke with two witnesses to the crash. a witness in a vehicle behind unit # 1 advised that unit # 1 was not traveling very fast when the pedestrian was struck. this witness advised that they did not look at the cross walk symbol at the time of the crash. another witness at the location who was on foot advised that it looked like the pedestrian ran out in front of the vehicle. this witness also did not look at the cross walk symbol at the time of the crash. witnesses: vehicle witness tracy neeper 214-717-3100on foot witness: john la farerra (subject is homeless and does not have a phone)

records.deidentified_narrative: mv1 was backing out of a parking space in a private parking lot. ped was unloading her grocery cart into the trunk of her unit. ped told me she felt the grocery cart hit her stomach and observed mv1 continue to back into the grocery cart pinning her between her unit and the grocery cart. ped told me she leaned over the cart as she remained pinned and began to hit the tailgate of mv1 attempting to get the attention of the driver of mv1. ped observed mv1 stop backing and traveled forward away from ped. ped observed mv1 travel a distance inside the parking lot and a wm passenger get out of mv1 and walk toward the back of mv1 to observe possible damage. then ped told me the wm passenger got back into mv1 and observed mv1 leave the parking lot. ped told me she believed mv1 was going to return to the crash location and provide information; however, mv1 did not return. i was able to observe survellance video from the crash and observed two males enter the vehicle and mv1 back into the grocery cart of ped and observed the impact of mv1 and the grocery cart crash and pin ped between her unit and the cart. while the crash occurred at a low rate of speed, ped experienced pain in the abdonimal region and was complaining of sharp pains an hour after the incident occurred. i requested ems to the location. ladder 51 treated ped and ped refused ems transport. ped's spouse showed up and i later called ped to get a status [medical facility] receiving treatment. mv1 driver was a wm 40-50 yo, 5'10"" 220 lbs, bald, bro goatee. he was wearing a blue tank with camo cargo shorts and gry tennis shoes. he also wore glasses. passenger of mv1 was a wm 15-20 yo, 6'1"" 200lbs. he was wearing a gry pokemon t-shirt and blue shorts. he had red and black slides on his feet and also had glasses. per det herries, l #2488, i will submit an afr offense report for failure to stop and provide information. dme on.

records.public_safe_text: mv1 was backing out of a parking space in a private parking lot. ped was unloading her grocery cart into the trunk of her unit. ped told me she felt the grocery cart hit her stomach and observed mv1 continue to back into the grocery cart pinning her between her unit and the grocery cart. ped told me she leaned over the cart as she remained pinned and began to hit the tailgate of mv1 attempting to get the attention of the driver of mv1. ped observed mv1 stop backing and traveled forward away from ped. ped observed mv1 travel a distance inside the parking lot and a wm passenger get out of mv1 and walk toward the back of mv1 to observe possible damage. then ped told me the wm passenger got back into mv1 and observed mv1 leave the parking lot. ped told me she believed mv1 was going to return to the crash location and provide information; however, mv1 did not return. i was able to observe survellance video from the crash and observed two males enter the vehicle and mv1 back into the grocery cart of ped and observed the impact of mv1 and the grocery cart crash and pin ped between her unit and the cart. while the crash occurred at a low rate of speed, ped experienced pain in the abdonimal region and was complaining of sharp pains an hour after the incident occurred. i requested ems to the location. ladder 51 treated ped and ped refused ems transport. ped's spouse showed up and i later called ped to get a status [medical facility] receiving treatment. mv1 driver was a wm 40-50 yo, 5'10"" 220 lbs, bald, bro goatee. he was wearing a blue tank with camo cargo shorts and gry tennis shoes. he also wore glasses. passenger of mv1 was a wm 15-20 yo, 6'1"" 200lbs. he was wearing a gry pokemon t-shirt and blue shorts. he had red and black slides on his feet and also had glasses. per det herries, l #2488, i will submit an afr offense report for failure to stop and provide information. dme on.
